title: Rabbi Avin, son of Rabbi Elazar
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:4, where he says of Saul’s enclosure, “There was a fence within a fence.” Hyman calls the attribution a scribal error and says to read it as at the end of Bamidbar Rabbah, chapter 4: Rabbi Avin in the name of Rabbi Elazar.

notes.text: The particular Midrash Rabbah book is not named. Hyman’s correction changes a father-son attribution into a report in Rabbi Elazar’s name.

The saved Torat Emet BamidbarRabbah4 final scalar’s complete connected sentence about Michal and Saul explicitly has Rabbi Avin in Rabbi Elazar’s name: Saul entered the sheep enclosure, a fence within a fence. This supports identifying the work and transmission alternative. The phrase does not say Saul himself was a fence. Hyman insists on a scribal correction; this is attributed at full force without proof of a print or manuscript history. The earlier Vayikra/Shemot nonmatches do not exclude this match. Only the complete1627char connected sentence and adjacent context were read from the29335char scalar, not the whole chapter.

In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:4, Rabbi Bun is styled “son of Rabbi Lazar,” and the fence surrounds the sheep enclosure. The parallel in Sukkah 5:4:4 gives Rabbi Abun in Rabbi Lazar’s name. Bamidbar Rabbah 4, near the end, gives Rabbi Avin in Rabbi Elazar’s name. These readings support the comparison Hyman makes, while the proposal that a scribe changed the wording is Hyman’s.
